title: Interstate branching deregulation and mortgage credit: Favara and Imbs (2015)
estimand: Effect of lifting one interstate branching restriction (Rice-Strahan index, 0-4) on the annual log growth of the number of mortgages originated in a county; one panel for banks (subject to the rules) and one for placebo lenders.
estimate_label: Effect on log growth of mortgage originations

options.label: Commercial banks
options.justification: FI Table 2 Panel A (baseline): banks are subject to branching rules.

options.label: Placebo lenders
options.justification: FI Table 2 Panel B: thrifts, credit unions and independent mortgage companies are not subject to the rules.

options.label: Contemporaneous index
options.justification: de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2024) re-estimate FI with the contemporaneous index.

options.label: Lagged any-deregulation dummy
options.justification: A binary coding avoids adding up qualitatively different restrictions.

options.label: Demand controls only
options.justification: A lagged outcome with county effects risks Nickell bias (FI addendum).

options.label: No controls
options.justification: de Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2024) re-estimate without controls; controls measured after deregulation may be outcomes.

options.label: Without 1995-1996 adopters
options.justification: Leave a cohort out (13 states): checks whether early adopters drive the estimate.

options.label: Without 2000-2001 adopters
options.justification: Leave a cohort out (4 states): late adopters serve as comparisons for most of the panel.

options.label: Without never-deregulated states
options.justification: Identify only from timing among adopters: the 8 states that never deregulated by 2005 may differ (Goodman-Bacon 2021).

options.label: Border counties
options.justification: FI Table A1: counties on state borders face similar local conditions.

options.label: Census region by year
options.justification: Regional housing and credit cycles in the late 1990s and 2000s.

reference.source: Favara and Imbs (2015), American Economic Review 105(3), Table 2, Panel A, column 1 (N = 10,992; 1,018 counties; 50 states)

notes: Cohorts are defined by each state's first year with any interstate branching deregulation (contemporaneous index). Clustered by state (50 clusters, fewer when a cohort is left out).
